dossier.headline: Jio Platforms listed at a large premium and then steadied
dossier.summary: The IPO was priced at ₹1,119, built from 1.43x on day one to 9.33x subscribed at close, and listed at ₹1,358. The stock gained about 27% over the issue price in its first two days, then traded flat in a ₹1,386.80–1,434.90 range in the third session, near ₹1,420. It has not appeared in a note since 30 October.
why_it_matters: The largest listing in the pipeline the notes track, and the reference point for the rest of it.
A strong listing shapes sentiment for the IPOs that follow.
QIB demand ran well ahead of the overall book at 4.13x on day one.

moved.name: Jio Platforms
moved.line: Listed at ₹1,358 against a ₹1,119 issue price, then steadied near ₹1,420.

watch: Whether the stock holds the listing premium once the first lock-ins pass.
Whether the reported December 2026 tariff hike lands as described.
questions: Does the listing premium hold once index inclusion flows settle?
How much of the subscription was anchor and QIB demand rather than retail?
conflicts: Sources differ on the day-one subscription close: 3.04x against 3.2x (note of 2026-10-22 1000).
The 15% December 2026 tariff hike comes from one report only (note of 2026-10-15 1230).
